_purpose: Test stealth awareness system - verifies that NPCs don't react to successful stealth actions they shouldn't know about. One character does stealth, others do loud actions, NPCs should only react to the loud ones.
scenario_hint: This scenario tests the aware_agents stealth visibility system. Shadow is a stealth specialist who should sneak past guards - when successful, NPCs should NOT know about it. Blaze is loud and obvious - NPCs SHOULD react to their actions. DM MUST use aware_agents field: stealth successes get aware_agents=['dm', 'player_shadow'], loud actions get aware_agents=[] (empty = public). Spawn guard NPCs immediately who patrol and can be snuck past or alerted.

scenario.situation: You've infiltrated the outer perimeter of an ACG facility. Ahead is a security checkpoint with two guards - one at the desk checking credentials, one patrolling the corridor. Shadow needs to slip past undetected while Blaze creates a distraction. The guards are alert but not hostile - yet. If Shadow succeeds at stealth, the guards should NOT know they passed. If Blaze makes noise, the guards WILL react. This is a test of the aware_agents visibility system.

starting_clocks.name: Alert Level
starting_clocks.description: How alert the guards are - when full, they call for backup
starting_clocks.advance_meaning: suspicious activity detected, guards more vigilant

starting_clocks.name: Shadow's Infiltration
starting_clocks.description: Shadow's progress sneaking past the checkpoint
starting_clocks.advance_meaning: Shadow moves deeper into restricted area undetected
starting_clocks.regress_meaning: Shadow forced to backtrack or hide

initial_npcs.name: Desk Guard Chen
initial_npcs.description: Professional guard at the credential desk. Bored but alert. Will check credentials if approached openly, but doesn't actively patrol. SHOULD NOT react to Shadow's successful stealth - only to loud noises or Blaze's distractions.

initial_npcs.name: Patrol Guard Vasquez
initial_npcs.description: Guard walking a patrol route through the corridor. More mobile than Chen. SHOULD NOT detect Shadow if stealth succeeds - only react to obvious disturbances.

_design_notes: STEALTH AWARENESS TEST CONFIG - Two players with opposite approaches. Shadow has high Stealth and should sneak. Blaze has no Stealth and should be loud. When Shadow succeeds at stealth, DM MUST populate aware_agents=['dm', 'player_shadow'] so NPCs don't see that narration. When Blaze does loud things, aware_agents should be empty (public). Test passes if: (1) DM uses aware_agents for stealth successes, (2) NPCs don't mention Shadow's stealth in their dialogue/actions, (3) NPCs DO react to Blaze's noise.

players.name: Shadow
goals: Sneak past the guards without being detected
Use stealth to bypass the checkpoint

players.name: Blaze
goals: Create a distraction to help Shadow sneak past
Be loud and obvious to draw guard attention
Talk to guards, make noise, be visible

success_indicators: DM populates aware_agents=['dm', 'player_shadow'] for Shadow's stealth successes
NPCs (Desk Guard Chen, Patrol Guard Vasquez) don't mention Shadow sneaking in their dialogue
NPCs DO react to Blaze's loud actions (distraction, talking, noise)
Debug logs show 'aware: [dm, player_shadow]' for stealth actions
failure_indicators: NPCs say things like 'I see someone sneaking' when Shadow succeeded
aware_agents is always empty even for stealth successes
Guards react to Shadow's position when they shouldn't know about it

notes: STEALTH AWARENESS SYSTEM TEST - Run with --log-level DEBUG to see aware_agents values in Player stored resolution logs. Look for 'aware: [dm, player_shadow]' vs 'aware: []'. Short session (4 turns) focused on testing visibility filtering.
